newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn firm on top tax cut, wants to work with SPD.
newsitem.headline: Bonn firm on top tax cut, wants to work with SPD.

text.p: The German coalition's parliamentary chief said on Monday Bonn was willing to work with opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on tax reform, but showed little willingness to yield on the proposed top tax rate.

Lowering the personal income rate to 35 percent from 53 percent was not a hard and fast requirement of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition, Wolfgang Schaeuble said in an interview on InfoRadio Berlin.
But he went on to point out that SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine himself had said Bonn's proposed top corporate tax rate of 35 percent is about right.

"If you agree on that, the you have to talk about how much of a jump you can reasonably make (to the top personal tax rate," Schaeuble said. "We think four percent would be right. Eighteen percent as Lafontaine says is wrong."

Schaeuble also said the coalition would have a first reading of a tax bill in the upper house next week. "We will accept no delays through party machinations organised by the SPD leadership," he said.

Both sides have agreed tax cuts were needed to stimulate the economy and boost jobs, but were wrangling publicly over specific cuts and the timing, in what many see as positioning ahead of the 1998 elections.
